title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. We have a family of curves X -> S with an open part U = X minus a divisor 'at infinity' T (the cusps), and a section-like datum: over each point s of S we have a point of the fibre X_s. Through the fundamental-group extension 1 -> pi -> E_{U} -> E_{base} -> 1 this point gives a section of the extension over the Galois group E_{K(s)}. Here pi is the geometric fundamental group of the fibre.

Previous page. On the open set S' where the point stays inside U, the composite E_K -> E_{U_K} -> E_U kills the inertia I_{s'}. One then gets a section E_{K(s)} -> E_{X_s} (more precisely into E_{U_s}). The complement D = S \ S' is purely of codimension 1: it is the image of the locus where the point runs into the cusp divisor T. Grothendieck introduces a mu_d-torsor attached to this degeneration.

This page.
(1) For a component D_alpha (the closure of a point s_alpha) of D, the relevant integer d is just the multiplicity of the divisor at D_alpha. Equivalently, it is the order of contact of the point with the cusp divisor.
(2) He now asks what happens for s in the union of the D_alpha. He fixes alpha and looks at the points specialising to the generic point s_alpha. Passing to the generic point, or to a suitable regular open subset of D_alpha, we again have a relative curve U_{D_alpha} over D_alpha. Hence an extension E_{U_{s_alpha}} of E_{K(s_alpha)} by pi, as for every point.
(3) The difference this time is that the geometric fibre no longer carries a k_alpha-rational point of U_{s_alpha}. There is only a point at infinity i_alpha in X_{s_alpha} \ U_{s_alpha}, which is now rational over k_alpha.
(4) But one still has, 'essentially canonically', a relative subgroup L_i of pi: the inertia (cusp) subgroup attached to i_alpha.

Next page. The section over s_alpha is a cuspidal ('tangential') section with image in the decomposition group of the cusp i_alpha. Its residual ambiguity is governed by the choice of a uniformiser of O_{S,s_alpha}, i.e. a local equation of D_alpha. That choice matters only through its class in m/m^2, i.e. through a trivialisation of the normal bundle N_{D_alpha/S}. The specialisation of these sections is then clear wherever the associated rational section of N_{D_alpha/S} is regular and invertible.

In modern terms. Grothendieck is computing the limit of a family of rational-point Galois sections of pi_1 as the point degenerates into a cusp along a divisor in the base. The limit is a cuspidal (tangential base point) section at the cusp. It depends on a normal vector to the boundary divisor D_alpha, refined by the contact multiplicity d: a mu_d-torsor, i.e. a d-th root of the normal datum.

Purpose. This serves the Longue Marche programme of understanding Galois sections and their specialisation (section-conjecture circle), and of studying the Teichmüller tower and its boundary.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that the limit section is canonical is hedged by Grothendieck himself ('de façon ess. canonique'). The dependence on the uniformiser / normal vector, and on a d-th root when d>1, is only resolved on the next page.
The canonicity of L_i as a subgroup of pi holds only up to conjugacy unless a base point / tangential path is fixed. Grothendieck glosses over this here.

ideas.what: As a family of rational points degenerates into a cusp along a boundary divisor D_alpha of the base, the associated Galois sections of pi_1 specialise to a cuspidal section. Its image lies in the decomposition group of the cusp i_alpha, which is rational over the residue field k_alpha.
ideas.modern_name: Limits of rational-point sections as cuspidal / tangential base point sections; degeneration of Galois sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Ihara, Nakamura (limits of Galois representations along degenerations, 1990s); cuspidal sections in Stix's book (2013)
ideas.where_published: Cuspidal sections are mentioned in the letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse discusses tangential base points informally; this specialisation computation itself is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: The limit section depends on the choice of a local equation of D_alpha only through the induced normal datum in m/m^2 = N^vee_{D_alpha/S}. When the contact multiplicity is d, it depends through a mu_d-torsor, i.e. a d-th root of that normal datum.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base point attached to a normal vector; higher-order contact / root-stack refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points); Nakamura and others for degeneration formulas; root stacks (Cadman, Abramovich–Graber–Vistoli) for the d-th root phenomenon

ideas.what: The degeneracy locus S \ S' is purely of codimension 1, with multiplicities given by the order of contact with the cusp divisor.
ideas.modern_name: Purity of the boundary divisor; pullback of the cusp divisor along a section

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly relates the limit cuspidal section to the normal bundle N_{D_alpha/S} of the boundary divisor in the base. He also ties the multiplicity d to a mu_d-torsor ambiguity. This gives a family version of 'tangential base points = limits of rational points', with a d-th root refinement for higher-order contact, which anticipates root-stack / log-geometric descriptions of degenerating sections.
missed.quote: on dispose d'un L_i ⊂ π relatif : c'est i_α, justement, de façon ess. canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Specialisation of Galois sections over higher-dimensional bases, as opposed to single degenerations, and the role of contact multiplicity are only partly treated in the section-conjecture literature (Stix, Nakamura, Wickelgren's work on cuspidal sections). This is a concrete, essentially complete local picture written in the mid-1980s.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes, but leaves aside as 'less urgent', the study of specialisation of these sections at the points of D_alpha where the normal-bundle section ceases to be regular and invertible. These are the higher-codimension strata and intersections of the D_alpha.
missed.quote: On peut se proposer d'étudier ce qui se passe aux autres points ... Mais cela me semble d'un intérêt moins brûlant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This concerns degenerations of sections at corners of the boundary, e.g. normal-crossing points in M_{g,n}-bar. It is relevant to Galois actions on Teichmüller groupoids and maximal degeneration (Nakamura).

deep.surprise_reason: The core idea, that cuspidal or tangential sections arise as limits of rational-point sections, is now standard (Deligne, Ihara–Nakamura, Stix). The explicit family version over a base, with dependence on the normal bundle of the boundary divisor and the mu_d refinement from contact multiplicity, is a nice unpublished detail. It is, however, not a striking new result.
transcription_corrections: 'E_{K(S_α)}' should read E_{K(s_α)} (lower-case s_α, generic point of D_α).
'comme tout pour s ∈ K' is doubtful; the image reads something like 'comme tout près / sur K', probably 'comme pour tout s', i.e. the generic situation of a relative curve.
'π - dédoublé[?]' is uncertain; the image suggests 'π - déduit' or 'π-dédié'. The sense is 'extension by π'.
'pt. rat. sur k[?]' should be 'pt. rat. sur k_α'. The following 'i.e. qui qui en pt' should be read as 'i.e. on n'a qu'un pt : l'infini i_α ∈ X_{s_α} \ U_{s_α}, maintenant rat. sur k_α'.
The final line contains the inserted phrase 'de façon ess. canonique' below 'justement'.
